title: 22 Fulani Men Found Executed in Mass Graves at Diafarabé — Malian Army and Dozo Militia Accused; Amnesty Calls for Investigation
detail: On May 15, 2026, a delegation of Diafarabé residents escorted by the military crossed to the south bank of the Niger River — where detained men had been taken on May 12 — and discovered 22 bodies in two mass graves. The victims were ethnic Fulani men aged 32–67 who had been attending a local cattle market in Diafarabé, a town in Mali's Mopti Region (Cercle de Tenenkou), on May 12, 2026. Survivors and witnesses reported that Malian soldiers and Dozo traditional hunters' militia had arrested at least 30 Fulani men at the market, bound and blindfolded them, transported them by canoe across the Niger River to the south bank, slit their throats, and buried them in mass graves. Eight men who were arrested were not found among the bodies; their fate is unknown. Amnesty International immediately called for an urgent, independent investigation, stating the killings appeared to constitute extrajudicial executions. FIDH (Fédération Internationale des Droits de l'Homme) joined the call for accountability. The Africa Report quoted a survivor: 'They slit their throats one by one.' The Malian junta has not issued a response. The incident follows the documented pattern of collective punishment against Fulani communities in Mali's central regions — including the 2022 Moura massacre (500+ killed, UN OHCHR documented), the 2019 Ogossagou massacre, and repeated HRW-documented incidents in which Fulani men at markets or cattle-grazing areas have been collectively arrested as presumptive JNIM suspects. The Diafarabé area — in the Tenenkou Cercle, Mopti Region — is core Katiba Macina territory; security forces frequently treat Fulani men in the area as JNIM sympathizers. The use of Dozo militia alongside regular troops is consistent with documented patterns across the Mopti-Ségou corridor. Amnesty International documented that Malian authorities have a history of conducting collective reprisals against communities in which JNIM fighters operate, making Fulani civilians doubly vulnerable — targeted by JNIM for cooperating with the state, and targeted by the state for being Fulani.

title: Bamako Blockade Ongoing — 3 of 6 Main Entry Roads Disrupted; Food and Fuel Prices Surge
detail: As of May 15, 2026, at least 3 of Bamako's 6 main road entry corridors remain disrupted by JNIM attacks on convoys, confirming that the April 28 'total siege' declaration remains operationally effective. Radio France Internationale (RFI) confirmed blockade activity at Soribougou (west), Naréna (southwest), and Ouélessébougou (south). Fuel and food prices are rising sharply across Bamako as JNIM's supply interdiction maintains structural pressure on the capital. The ongoing blockade — now 17 days after the April 28 formal JNIM declaration — demonstrates that the May 2 convoy of 800+ trucks was a temporary breakthrough rather than a structural resolution: JNIM retains the ability to obstruct supply routes at will. The Manantali power grid sabotage (May 12) has added an electricity dimension to the existing fuel and food crisis. JNIM's siege strategy has progressed through four distinct phases: road fuel blockade (Jan–April 2026) → total siege declaration (April 28) → prison assault + convoy arson (May 6–7) → power grid attack (May 12). Each phase has progressively escalated the multi-domain pressure on Bamako's essential services without triggering a militarily effective FAMa ground response.
